content.p: Packaging: one command from checkout to running
RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app
Multi-stage build: the image that runs carries only the JRE and the jar - no build tools. The app runs as a non-root user by default.

li.p: docker-compose: two profiles - gateway alone, or gateway + the Mountebank simulator.
CI (GitHub Actions): clean build, all 45 tests, JaCoCo gates - line 80%, branch 70%. A regression fails the merge.
Run it: docker compose --profile bank up --build - app on :8080, Swagger on /swagger-ui/index.html.
Everything in the repo: build, tests, runtime, and the bank simulator agree on one command.

content.p: Packaging is the part that makes this exercise runnable by anyone. The Dockerfile is a multi-stage build: the first stage compiles, the second stage copies only the jar into a slim JRE image, and the app runs as a non-root user. Docker Compose provides two profiles - the gateway alone, or the gateway plus the Mountebank bank simulator - so one command starts the whole system. CI runs the full build with coverage gates, meaning a regression fails before it merges.
